title: Simple and compound interest, two years

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: own numbers, story and explanation; no text from any question bank.

stem: Asha keeps ₹{{p}} in a bank for 2 years at {{r}}% a year. How many rupees more does she earn if interest is compounded yearly instead of simple? Type the number.
explanation:
### Understand
Same principal, rate and time; only the way interest is counted differs. We want CI − SI for 2 years.

### Plan
In year 2, compound interest also earns interest on year 1's interest. So for 2 years, CI − SI = P × (r/100)².

### Solve
1. Year-1 interest: {{p}} × {{r}}/100 = {{i1}}.
2. Interest on that in year 2: {{i1}} × {{r}}/100 = {{d}}.
3. CI − SI = **{{d}}** rupees.

### Check
P(r/100)² = {{p}} × {{r}}² / 10,000 = {{d}}. The difference is small next to the interest itself ({{i1}} a year), as it should be for 2 years.
shortcut: 2 years: CI − SI = P(r/100)². 3 years: P(r/100)²(3 + r/100).
solver:
import json, sys
from fractions import Fraction as F
p = json.load(sys.stdin)
P, r = p["p"], p["r"]
i1 = F(P * r, 100); d = i1 * r / 100
f = lambda x: int(x) if x.denominator == 1 else float(x)
print(json.dumps({"answer": f(d), "values": {"i1": f(i1), "d": f(d)}}))

revision_card.back: P × (r/100)². It is the interest earned on year 1's interest.
